head_commit.message:
fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry (#930)

* fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry

The first real release run uploaded 474 debug files per matrix leg, ~1900 per
release: dependency build scripts, proc-macro .so files, ring/aws-lc-sys
object files, and every third-party system library bundled into the AppImage —
all to symbolicate one binary. Cause was pointing sentry-cli at the whole
target/ tree.

Scope it to the ajh_tauri* artifacts under release/deps. The paths come from
that run's logs rather than inference, which mattered: on every platform the
debug artifacts use the LIBRARY name (ajh_tauri, underscore) and live in
deps/, not the bin name at release/ajh-tauri. A guessed
release/ajh-tauri.dSYM would have missed the macOS debug companion entirely
and uploaded a binary with no symbols.

Guard the per-triple directory behind a non-empty check — with no triple the
path collapses to the same dir and enumerates everything twice. Verified by
simulating all three layouts: 2 files each, debug companion included, and an
empty match still fails loudly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: assert the debug companion is present, not just some artifact

Review noted the empty-check proves some ajh_tauri* file was found, not that
the file needed to symbolicate the shipped binary is there. Finding
ajh_tauri.exe while its .pdb is missing would pass and still ship
unresolvable stack traces — the same looks-fine-reports-nothing shape this
feature keeps producing.

Assert the companion each platform actually emits, taken from the release
run's uploaded-file list rather than assumed: .pdb on Windows, .dSYM on
macOS, and nothing on Linux where DWARF stays inside the binary. Verified the
positive and negative case for each.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix: fail the release when a configured sentry symbol upload breaks (#929)

* fix: fail the release when a configured sentry symbol upload breaks

The symbol upload was continue-on-error, so a wrong token or a rejected
upload would skip silently and the first anyone would know is a crash report
full of bare addresses. That is the same silent-failure mode this feature was
reviewed for three times.

Drop continue-on-error and add set -euo pipefail so a failure past the guard
turns the run red. Move the step after Upload Release Assets so the installers
are already published — a Sentry outage should not cost a release, but it
should still be visible.

Absent secrets stay a legitimate skip for forks and pre-provisioning releases,
now surfaced as a warning annotation instead of a plain log line, so "not
configured" stays distinguishable from "configured wrong".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make the symbol upload loud without breaking the updater

The review gate caught that hard-failing the step cascades. It sits in a
4-leg matrix, and generate-update-manifest, update-cask and
update-download-page all hang off a bare needs: build — so a Sentry hiccup on
one leg flips the aggregate result and skips all three. latest.json is never
written and auto-update breaks for every existing user, while the installers
sit attached to the release. That is a far worse failure than unresolved
stack traces, and the opposite of the stated intent.

Restore continue-on-error and surface failure through an ::error:: annotation
plus a step-summary entry instead. Loud, unmissable, and non-gating.

Not taking the gate's other suggestion of loosening the downstream jobs to
if: always(): that would publish an updater manifest even when a platform's
build genuinely failed, pointing users at artifacts that do not exist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: keep adr-0020 to the decision and point at the workflow

CodeRabbit flagged the symbol-upload bullet for duplicating the workflow's

head_commit.message:
feat: add opt-out crash reporting via sentry (#927)

* feat: add opt-out crash reporting via sentry

The app was blind in production. The panic hook wrote crashes.log and the
diagnostics zip could export it, but both needed the user to notice a failure
and file an issue by hand. React errors caught by a boundary never reached the
window at all, so they were invisible even in principle.

Desktop app only. The extension keeps its AMO data_collection_permissions of
['none'] and the landing site keeps its no-third-party-JS origin invariant.

Consent is Rust-owned rather than a renderer preference: sentry::init has to run
before tauri::Builder, because sentry-rust-minidump forks the crash-reporter
process at startup and panic = "abort" leaves nothing in-process able to flush a
crash. There is no WebView at that point, so no localStorage to read.

Transmission requires enabled && consentShown, not just enabled. The default is
on, but nothing is sent until the setup wizard has actually shown the choice — a
default nobody saw is not consent, and that gap is where privacy claims break.
A user who never finishes onboarding never reports anything.

Every outgoing event is serialized, passed through the same redact_token
pipeline the diagnostics bundle uses, and deserialized — whole-event rather than
field-by-field, because a field list is a denylist that rots as the SDK adds
fields. send_default_pii is off and server_name is overridden, since the SDK
otherwise sends the machine hostname.

The DSN is baked by build.rs from an env var set only in the signed release job
and read with option_env!, so local builds, contributor clones and every CI
check compile to None and cannot transmit.

This reverses a published promise: the privacy policy named Sentry as absent in
three places and ADR-0005 defined the boundary as "no telemetry". ADR-0005 gains
an eighth egress class, ADR-0020 records the decision, and all twelve claim
sites are rewritten — including Footer.tsx, whose "no server-side copy, deleting
locally deletes it everywhere" became false, and /privacy, which is the policy
URL filed with both stores and now separates desktop collection from extension
non-collection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: classify the crash-reporting module in the architecture layers

The architecture test caught it unclassified. Shell layer rather than lower: it
is constructed by lib::run() before the Tauri builder exists, and it reaches
down into commands::support::redact_lines to reuse the diagnostics redactor
instead of growing a second, weaker one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: resolve the crash-reporting consent directory exactly once

Review found the feature could never activate. init() ran before
tauri::Builder and resolved the consent file through
platform::config::data_dir(), which at that moment falls back to $HOME/.ajh
